details:
LUNARIS: Lunar Landing Site Navigator

LUNARIS is a prototype for exploring lighting and Earth visibility at candidate lunar locations. Choose a coordinate and UTC date to see hourly Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation estimates from NASA/JPL Horizons. The interface also shows illustrative candidate comparison scores to help frame early site-screening questions.

How it works
The browser interface sends a request through the included Python proxy to NASA/JPL Horizons. Horizons supplies the Sun and Earth position data for the selected lunar coordinates and date. The prototype displays the hourly profile and lets users download a scenario record.

Data and limits
NASA/JPL Horizons is used for the ephemeris estimates. The candidate comparison scores are illustrative interface values; they are not calculated from the Horizons results and do not represent sunlight duration, communications availability, terrain clearance, or landing safety. The prototype does not include a terrain horizon mask or validated mission-planning model. Treat it as an exploratory concept, not an operational tool.
